$comment: PHASE 2/3 · deployment config for BOTH sellable products.
OWNER DECISIONS: 1a · 2a · 3a · 4a · 5a. PREPARE ONLY — NOT DEPLOYED.
ONE FILE, TWO PROJECTS. Both Vercel projects use Root Directory
`apps/nivxray-xdr`, so they both read THIS file. That is why the
product boundary is expressed as HOST-CONDITIONAL redirects rather
than per-project settings — a per-project build command could not
distinguish the two, but `has: [{type: host}]` can.
Project A · xdr.nivxforge.com · / → /xdr · /edr/* → EDR host
Project B · edr.nivxforge.com · / → /edr · /xdr/* → XDR host
WHY THE GUARD EXISTS: XDR and EDR currently ship in ONE bundle (60
routes, 13 of them /edr/*) and the app's catch-all is
`<Route path="*" element={<Navigate to="/xdr" replace/>} />`.
Without these rules, `edr.nivxforge.com/` would land the analyst on
/xdr/incidents — XDR served from the EDR hostname, i.e. exactly the
'silently falls back into the wrong product' failure the owner
prohibited.
COVERAGE, STATED HONESTLY: these are SERVER redirects, so they fire
on every real navigation — typed URL, external link, bookmark, hard
refresh, any full page load. They CANNOT fire on client-side React
navigation that happens after the page is already loaded, because no
HTTP request is made. That residual gap is documented in
memory/PHASE2_3_XDR_EDR_DEPLOYMENT_PREP.md with a proposed fix
awaiting owner approval; it self-heals on refresh.
ORDER MATTERS: cross-host rules come FIRST so the `/` landing rules
cannot shadow them. Both the bare path and the `:path*` form are
listed rather than relying on `:path*` also matching the bare path.
permanent:false (307) is deliberate — a 308 would be cached by
browsers and is the wrong tool while a topology is still moving.
PREVIEW / *.vercel.app HOSTS ARE UNAFFECTED: no `has` condition
matches them, so no redirect fires and the app behaves exactly as it
does today (productOrigins SAME_ORIGIN mode). The guard is keyed to
the two production hostnames only, which keeps Preview XDR and
Preview EDR working untouched.
ENV: set REACT_APP_NIVXRAY_API_URL per project in the Vercel
dashboard. Unlike the CRA Workspace app, this one has no dotenv
precedence trap — vite.config.js uses loadEnv(mode, cwd, ""), and a
real environment variable was PROVEN to override .env (build emitted
4 production API refs and 0 preview refs). Leave REACT_APP_XDR_URL,
REACT_APP_EDR_URL and REACT_APP_WORKSPACE_URL UNSET (owner decision
4a) so no launcher points at an unverified product.
